target: Internal atomic storage, scheduler mechanics, Environment install coordination, exchange mechanics, cloud application assembly, immutable Environment stores, CLI ownership, and test infrastructure.
primary_semantics: Complete R1 through R8 as behavior-preserving modularization: move each mechanism to one canonical Owner while preserving every public and persisted contract.
invariants: Raw archives and all authoritative persisted records remain byte-for-byte unchanged by the refactor.
No storage migration, protocol revision, feature, default, security policy, permission expansion, or model behavior change is part of this work.
Capture Core remains independent and no R1-R8 work may add AI, Exchange, Environment, UI, or Control behavior to it.
Rule and Skill installation retain separate recovery and rollback failure domains.
Archive, Environment, Evidence, and Attachment streams retain separate state and failure domains.
CLI and dashboard observable behavior remains compatible.
allowed_changes: Add internal Platform Foundation, Application Service, Environment, Exchange, domain-owner, and test-support modules.
Move or delegate existing behavior behind compatibility facades.
Delete duplicate implementations only after all callers use the canonical owner and parity tests pass.
prohibited_changes: Change version numbers, release metadata, installation state, running schedulers, desktop shortcuts, or published artifacts.
Change archive, summary, index, Environment, project package, cloud envelope, or cursor formats.
Combine independent ledgers, cursors, acknowledgements, rollback stores, recovery engines, or security validators.
Claim a stage passed from mocks or file existence alone when its contract requires exact bytes or state transition evidence.
before_after_checks: Compare exact atomic-write bytes, modes, failure order, and destination state before and after R1.
Compare exact plist/XML/wrapper bytes and scheduler runner calls before and after R2.
Compare complete Rule and Skill journal, receipt, rollback, mode, recovery, and error results before and after R3.
Compare all four stream manifests, payloads, cursors, predecessor chains, authentication results, and failure isolation before and after R4.
Compare CLI and dashboard cloud status, configure, enable, disable, and sync responses before and after R5.
Compare Governance and Evolution envelope, event, replica, and validation bytes before and after R6.
Compare all CLI commands, help, arguments, defaults, lock policy, exit codes, stdout, and stderr before and after R7.
Compare test discovery IDs and required rehearsal scenario coverage before and after R8.
